# S23 — Lock ID allocation with flock

Two `adj ask` runs at the same instant in one checkout, with different titles,
can both take the same ID (C62/C64). The owner decided to close that window with
an advisory `flock` held across "scan IDs, then link the file" in
`store.Create`.

**Findings:** Owner decision 2026-10-15 (S05 review MEDIUM-2; C62, C64) · **Size:** M · **Tree:** store
Cites: C114 decision: ID allocation is locked with flock, C62 decision: Store writes go through a synced temp file: Update renames it over the record, Create links it into place and never replaces a file, C64 decision: Permissions and retry: new records are 0644, Update keeps the old file's permission bits, and Create retries up to three times when its file name is taken, C32 decision: Standing rule: implementer decides unfixed interface details, C24 decision: Runtime: Go, standard library only

**Not in this slice:** collisions from separate branches or clones (lint and
renumber, S14/S15, handle those; a lock cannot); Windows locking beyond a
documented fallback; locking `Update` (it rewrites one existing file by rename
and needs no ID).

## Why

Owner decision 2026-10-15 after the S05 review: the bounded retry (C64) only
catches same-path collisions, so concurrent creates with different slugs still
produce duplicate IDs. A lock serialises ID allocation inside one checkout.

## Files

- `internal/store/lock_unix.go` (build tag `unix`): acquire and release an
  exclusive `syscall.Flock` on a lock file in the store directory.
- `internal/store/lock_other.go` (build tag `!unix`): the fallback the
  implementer decides and records (C32), for example no lock plus the existing
  retry, documented.
- `internal/store/store.go`: `Create` holds the lock from the ID scan through
  the link.
- `internal/store/lock_test.go`.
- `AGENTS.md` (Store and config) and the C62/C64 catalog text.

## Failing tests

- Two goroutines (or two `Store` values on one directory) each call `Create`
  with different titles while a test hook (like `beforeLink`, C64) holds the
  first one between scan and link: the second blocks until the first finishes,
  and the two records get different IDs. Without the lock the hook shows both
  taking the same ID.
- The lock file is created inside the store directory, is not a record (scan
  ignores it, C59) and is not left holding the lock after `Create` returns,
  including when `Create` fails (invalid record, link error).
- A lock that cannot be taken in time returns an error naming the lock file
  (the timeout or non-blocking behaviour is the implementer's choice, C32), and
  writes no record.
- Tests stay inside `t.TempDir()` stores and use no real concurrency beyond
  what the hook controls; no sleeps longer than the test needs.

## Implement

Implementer decides and records each of these (C32):

- lock file name (proposed `.adj.lock`, a dot-file so scan ignores it, and
  whether to add it to the store's gitignore guidance);
- blocking `LOCK_EX` versus `LOCK_EX|LOCK_NB` with a bounded retry or timeout;
- the non-unix fallback;
- whether `beforeLink`-style hooks extend to the lock for tests.

Keep the bounded retry from C64 as a second line of defence. Go standard library
only (C24): `syscall.Flock` under a `unix` build tag.
